idea-plugin.name: GH Stack
idea-plugin.description:
A thin IntelliJ wrapper around the GitHub CLI gh stack extension. View and navigate stacked pull requests without leaving the IDE.

  • View the current stacked PR chain in a dedicated GH Stack tool window; the view refreshes automatically as branches and Git state change
  • See the stack as a commit graph, with each layer's PR number, plus its merged / queued / needs-rebase status and the current branch
  • Check out a specific layer
  • Copy the selected branch name from the stack list with Ctrl/Command+C
  • Rename a layer's branch from its context menu and re-initialize the stack locally, keeping the other layers and their pull requests as they are
  • Add a branch on top of the stack
  • Initialize a new stack
  • Rebase the stack (whole, upstack, downstack, or without trunk), then continue, abort, or cancel a running rebase
  • Rebase from any layer upward by right-clicking it in the stack list
  • Optionally stash uncommitted changes and untracked files around a rebase (ask / always / never)
  • Prompt to enable git rerere before initializing or rebasing a stack, so repeated conflict resolutions are reused
  • Switch between locally tracked stacks from the All stacks column beside the current stack
  • Prune a dangling local stack whose branches are all gone from the All stacks context menu
  • Follow the repository of the file selected in the editor, or pin the panel to the project repository, a Git submodule, or another Git root
  • Show clear next steps when gh or the gh stack extension is missing, or the current branch is not in a stack
  • Log every gh command the plugin runs, with its output and exit code, in the Console tab of the GH Stack tool window
  • Configure the gh executable path and how much the console logs in Settings | Tools | GH Stack

Requires GitHub CLI, gh extension install github/gh-stack, and a signed-in account (gh auth login).
